newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Inv Bank to raise capital to 2.2 bln lev.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Inv Bank to raise capital to 2.2 bln lev.

text.p: The private Bulgarian Investment Bank (BIB) decided to raise capital to 2.2 billion levs from 800 million levs through a new share issue, the bank's legal adviser Teodora Shipkova said on Tuesday.
"The shareholders' meeting decided late on Monday to raise the bank's capital to 2.2 billion levs to meet central bank's licensing requirements," he told Reuters.
Shipkova added that all of the bank's shareholders were expected to subscribe shares from the new issue in proportion to their current equity.
The BIB was set two years ago as part of a project supported by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), which holds 35 percent of its capital.
Banque Nationale de Paris owns five percent, Commercial Bank of Greece 17.7 percent, the Legist Jersey Trustee Limited 11 percent and the remainder is held among several Bulgarian banks.

The state-owned Balkanbank and the private Trade and Savings Bank, which have 2.5 percent and 4.4 percent equity in BIB respectively, were among the nine banks put under special supervision by the central bank on September 23.

In August the central bank raised minimum capital requirements for banks to 1.4 billion levs levs for a domestic licence and to 2.2 billion levs for a full one due to the sharp fall of the lev on the domestic forex market.
The requirements are to be met by the end of March 1997.
